claim: Of every 100 participants in genome-wide studies, up to 2021

source.citation: Fatumo S, Chikowore T, Choudhury A, Ayub M, Martin AR, Kuchenbaecker K. A roadmap to increase diversity in genomic studies. Nature Medicine 28(2):243–250 (2022).

locators.shares: Main text, section 1.0: European descent 86.3%, followed by East Asian 5.9%, African 1.1%, South Asian 0.8% and Hispanic/Latino 0.08%; studies with multiple ancestries 4.8%.
locators.catalog_date: Figure 1 legend: the proportion of samples from individuals cumulatively reported by the GWAS Catalog as of July 8, 2021.
locators.diversity: Main text: African populations have the most genetic diversity, followed by South Asians.

unit: participants (samples from individuals) reported by the GWAS Catalog, counted once per study and not deduplicated
remainder: Other or not reported: what the listed shares leave of 100% (1.02%).
rounding: Largest remainder over the three drawn groups (European ancestry, African ancestry, and all other ancestries or not recorded) to whole people out of 100.
verified: 2026-10-14: shares, date and diversity sentence checked against the author manuscript (LSHTM repository) and the PMC copy (PMC7614889); citation metadata from the PMC record.
